How Fit and P(Fit≥100) differ

Fit is the average level-11 archetype score across simulated development outcomes. It is a score, not a probability, and may exceed 100%.

P(Fit≥100) is the percentage of those simulated outcomes whose final Fit reaches or exceeds 100%. It can differ from the average because outcomes vary around that average.

The expected Fit is exactly 100%. Current values: Fit 100.0%; P(Fit≥100) 100.0%.

FIT DEVELOPMENT — LEVEL 11 (optimized stat allocation)

How stat allocation is optimized

Only the archetype's Fit stats shown in Target Profile are eligible. At every future level-up through level 11, the projection develops all eligible stats when there are three or fewer; otherwise it chooses the three expected to produce the highest final Fit for this archetype.

Talent stars shape each stat's possible roll range. Archetype baselines, targets, weights, and any Fit-only ceilings determine how valuable each gain is. Exact permanent trait and permanent-injury effects are included in the projected profile. Owned perks do not alter this natural-stat projection; their supported exact effects are shown only in effective current stats.

This is an optimized development policy, not a guaranteed outcome or a claim that every roll will be maximal. Temporary injuries and quarantined FutureRolls do not drive normal projection choices.

P(Fit≥100) is the percentage of those simulated outcomes whose final Fit reaches or exceeds 100%. It can differ from the average because outcomes vary around that average.

The expected Fit is below 100%. Current values: Fit 0.0%; P(Fit≥100) 0.0%.

FIT DEVELOPMENT — LEVEL 11 (optimized stat allocation)

How stat allocation is optimized

Only the archetype's Fit stats shown in Target Profile are eligible. At every future level-up through level 11, the projection develops all eligible stats when there are three or fewer; otherwise it chooses the three expected to produce the highest final Fit for this archetype.

Talent stars shape each stat's possible roll range. Archetype baselines, targets, weights, and any Fit-only ceilings determine how valuable each gain is. Exact permanent trait and permanent-injury effects are included in the projected profile. Owned perks do not alter this natural-stat projection; their supported exact effects are shown only in effective current stats.

This is an optimized development policy, not a guaranteed outcome or a claim that every roll will be maximal. Temporary injuries and quarantined FutureRolls do not drive normal projection choices.

Talent stars shape each stat's possible roll range. Archetype baselines, targets, weights, and any Fit-only ceilings determine how valuable each gain is. Exact permanent trait and permanent-injury effects are included in the projected profile. Owned perks do not alter this natural-stat projection; their supported exact effects are shown only in effective current stats.

This is an optimized development policy, not a guaranteed outcome or a claim that every roll will be maximal. Temporary injuries and quarantined FutureRolls do not drive normal projection choices.

How Fit and P(Fit≥100) differ

Fit is the average level-11 archetype score across simulated development outcomes. It is a score, not a probability, and may exceed 100%.

P(Fit≥100) is the percentage of those simulated outcomes whose final Fit reaches or exceeds 100%. It can differ from the average because outcomes vary around that average.

The expected Fit is below 100%. Current values: Fit 0.0%; P(Fit≥100) 0.0%.

FIT DEVELOPMENT — LEVEL 11 (optimized stat allocation)

How stat allocation is optimized

Only the archetype's Fit stats shown in Target Profile are eligible. At every future level-up through level 11, the projection develops all eligible stats when there are three or fewer; otherwise it chooses the three expected to produce the highest final Fit for this archetype.

Talent stars shape each stat's possible roll range. Archetype baselines, targets, weights, and any Fit-only ceilings determine how valuable each gain is. Exact permanent trait and permanent-injury effects are included in the projected profile. Owned perks do not alter this natural-stat projection; their supported exact effects are shown only in effective current stats.

This is an optimized development policy, not a guaranteed outcome or a claim that every roll will be maximal. Temporary injuries and quarantined FutureRolls do not drive normal projection choices.

Only the archetype's Fit stats shown in Target Profile are eligible. At every future level-up through level 11, the projection develops all eligible stats when there are three or fewer; otherwise it chooses the three expected to produce the highest final Fit for this archetype.

Talent stars shape each stat's possible roll range. Archetype baselines, targets, weights, and any Fit-only ceilings determine how valuable each gain is. Exact permanent trait and permanent-injury effects are included in the projected profile. Owned perks do not alter this natural-stat projection; their supported exact effects are shown only in effective current stats.

This is an optimized development policy, not a guaranteed outcome or a claim that every roll will be maximal. Temporary injuries and quarantined FutureRolls do not drive normal projection choices.

How Fit and P(Fit≥100) differ

Fit is the average level-11 archetype score across simulated development outcomes. It is a score, not a probability, and may exceed 100%.

P(Fit≥100) is the percentage of those simulated outcomes whose final Fit reaches or exceeds 100%. It can differ from the average because outcomes vary around that average.

The expected Fit is below 100%. Current values: Fit 0.0%; P(Fit≥100) 0.0%.
